content.comment_body: I'm attempting to calibrate an analog sensor output, which should measure between 6 and 144 inches using a 4-20mA signal. The closest I have achieved is setting the gain to 0.14 and the offset to 6, resulting in a minimum reading of 6 and a maximum of 146. My setup includes an analog amplifier that scales the signal from 0 to 1000, and then I perform a secondary scaling to achieve the above numbers, but I can't reach the desired range precisely.
Please avoid submitting multiple posts for the same issue.

This thread is closed because the question was submitted twice. The duplicate post titled '4-20mA to 6-144 inches using [product_name]' appeared in the conference [product_name] - Hardware. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user is having trouble precisely scaling a 4-20mA sensor output to the intended 6-144 inch range using an analog module. Adjusting gain and offset parameters doesn’t result in a perfect match, as the output overshoots the maximum value. This highlights a common challenge with analog input modules relating to accurate input signal scaling.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to be able to configure scaling parameters through the module or software so that the 4-20mA input is exactly mapped to the 6-144 inch measurement range.
